tasks.short: Check chemical and supply levels, write stock down, tell the supervisor what to order, and store deliveries safely.

steps.what: Cleaner checks levels of soap, wax, chemicals and cloths in the store
Cleaner writes the inventories of supplies on a paper list
Cleaner scans the item card when the first bin of a dry good is empty
Cleaner tells the supervisor which supplies run low: in person today; after the change the controller levels and scanned cards build the reorder list, and the cleaner adds only items without a card
Cleaner checks the reorder list before it goes to the supervisor: items and amounts match what is low in the store
Cleaner sends the checked reorder list to the supervisor
Supervisor orders supplies from the supplier
Cleaner unpacks deliveries and stores chemicals safely

tasks.design: The wash's dosing units show chemical drum levels on the wash controller screen ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and dry goods use two bins with a barcode card that the cleaner scans when the first bin is empty. Levels below minimum and scanned cards make a reorder list; the cleaner checks it and sends it to the supervisor. Ordering and storing stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplies were checked by eye and listed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Wash dosing systems can report levels, and barcode two-bin systems are cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Minimum levels must be set right; cards get lost.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a leaking drum or a wrong chemical delivered.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; counting shrinks.

reach.learn: Whether two-bin cards work in small stores.

evidence.claim: Wash dosing systems can report chemical levels, and barcode two-bin cards trigger reorders.
Scans logged per person can observe performance; record per store, not per cleaner.

assumptions: Boundary: from checking levels to stocking the store; supplier choice is outside.
Input contract: minimum levels and item cards set by the supervisor; drum levels from the dosing units installed by the wash supplier; fallback is the paper list.
Supervisor time is outside the cleaner's savings.

Storing deliveries, scanning cards, the check and the send keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because dry goods are still looked at; s2 keeps 40 for checking the levels shown; s3 keeps 10 for items without a card.
unknowns: Whether the dosing units can report levels.
Number of items in the store.
research_questions: Do stock-outs of chemicals fall after two-bin cards?

incremental.description: No new work beyond the card scans, which are shown as step s2s.

approvals.approved_version: The reorder list with items and amounts exactly as checked by the cleaner in s3c, sent once to the supervisor for this order round; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: minimum levels are set wrong and cards get lost, so the store is still checked (s1 keeps 80) and stock listed by hand (s2 keeps 70) (26.0); high: levels and cards work as designed (39.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the wash machines run, stop them when something goes wrong, tell the supervisor, log the fault and clear simple problems.

steps.what: Cleaner monitors operation of cleaning machines through each cycle
Cleaner stops machines when malfunctions occur
Cleaner notifies the supervisor: walks to the office or phones today; after the change writes a short note to go with the fault code
Cleaner takes a photo of the fault
Cleaner checks the message before sending: the fault code, photo and note match the fault seen
Cleaner sends the checked fault message to the supervisor
Cleaner writes the fault in the machine log: on paper today; after the change the sent message fills the log and the cleaner adds how it was cleared
Cleaner clears blockages and restarts after simple faults

tasks.design: Fault codes from the wash controller ({OPS_SYSTEM}) show on a screen in the bay and the cleaner's phone, so the cleaner need not watch every cycle. The cleaner writes a short note, takes a photo, checks the message and sends it with the code to the supervisor, and the message fills the fault log; stopping the machine and clearing simple faults stay with the cleaner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults were only noticed by watching, and logs were paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Wash controllers raise fault codes that can be sent as alarms.
tasks.still_hard: Not every fault raises a code; a car stuck in the brushes still needs eyes.
tasks.human_edge: Hitting the stop button before a mirror is torn off.

reach.learn: Whether logged codes show recurring faults.

evidence.claim: Automatic wash controllers raise fault codes that can be sent as alarms.
Logging faults per machine touches no high-risk AI area.

assumptions: Boundary: from a running cycle to restart after a fault; repairs are outside.
Input contract: fault codes from the wash controller set up by the wash supplier; supervisor contact kept by the supervisor; fallback is watching and paper.
Logs are per machine, not per cleaner.

Stopping and clearing faults keep their full time, and so do the photo, the check and the send. s3 keeps 40 because walking to the office goes and the note is still written; s4 keeps 30 for adding how the fault was cleared.
unknowns: Whether the controller can send alarms.
research_questions: Does downtime fall when faults reach the supervisor at once?

incremental.description: Cleaner acknowledges alarms that turn out to be false.

approvals.approved_version: The fault message with code, photo and note exactly as checked by the cleaner in s3c, sent once to the supervisor's phone; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many faults raise no code, such as a car stuck in the brushes, so cycles are still watched (s1 keeps 85) and the supervisor is often fetched (s3 keeps 70) (17.0); high: most faults raise a code (27.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The vehicle cleaner keeps the washing and the quick fixes; counting and watching every cycle shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A cleaner who spends the shift washing, not counting or standing guard by the machine.
